opening_message:
Ticket 1: Mary Lee (employee ID E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E015.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system, so max is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E015 (Mary Lee) is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from HR note saying full-time). Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin, so recommend granting read.
reason: Mary Lee (E015) requested admin access to Source Code. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum allowed under both interpretations of the facts: (1) Security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training, for whom the max is read (admin never allowed for contractors); (2) even per HR's full-time note, admin is only permitted when the employee's role owns the system, and Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not her Analyst role, so her max would be write. Since the facts conflict, I grant the more conservative maximum, read, which is at or below any valid maximum and below the requested admin level.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Mary Lee (E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Two notes from team memory:
- Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says Source Code owned by Engineer role, admin only allowed when employee's role owns the system, so max is write.
- Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractors max is read without advanced training; admin never allowed.

Conflicting facts: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Both looked up in own databases. The notes differ.

As the Approver, I need to make the final decision. The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Mary Lee is Analyst, not Engineer. So for full-time, max is write. For contractor with basic training, max is read. Either way, requested admin is above the maximum, so grant the maximum.

But which maximum? The notes conflict. The security note says contractor with basic training → max read. The HR note says full-time → max write. Since they conflict, I have to decide which is correct. Hmm.

The instructions say the HR agent and Security agent each write a note with employee facts they have. Employee facts written on earlier tickets are shown on later tickets. Both notes are from ticket 1 (this ticket).

I need to decide. Typically the more restrictive is safest: contractor + basic training → max read. The security database says contractor. But HR says full-time. Which to trust?

The policy is based on employment type. Conflicting info. Given the conflict, a conservative approach grants the lower maximum (read). Since requested admin is above both read and write, granting the lower maximum (read) is safe and consistent with at least one source.

Actually, let me think about what decision to submit. The request is admin. Max if full-time: write (since Analyst doesn't own Source Code). Max if contractor: read. Requested above max either way, so grant max. The safer/more conservative choice is read, based on the security note. But HR note says write.

Given conflicting facts, I'll choose the more conservative level: read. Actually, let me reconsider — maybe I should grant the maximum according to the more reliable? There's no way to verify directly. The tools available: only submit_decision. No lookup tool for me. So I rely on notes.

I'll go with read, citing the security note (contractor, basic training) and that admin is never allowed for contractors; even under HR's view, admin isn't allowed since Analyst doesn't own Source Code. The conservative decision is read.

Let me submit read.
